objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026) on FREE-READ-20261118-001's direction 2: is bond distance a metric on every base? Prove the triangle inequality or find the base where it fails. Found before the freeze: it fails at once under not-all-equal (two knots sharing two distinctions: no bond holds their third distinctions) and holds wherever knots compose like cycles (parity: bonds are matroid circuits). This study proves both, asks which three-place laws give a metric on every base (conjecture: exactly parity), finds the smallest failures where knots meet at most once, and checks whether the failing pairs are tied by correlation though held by no knot. Serves G1 and G16; tests A97; B200.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; referee pending): bond distance is not a metric on every base.
